source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:41 ('ברכו — the resh with sheva ALONE, as our custom')
claim_en: THE HALF-VOWEL LAW, STATION 8 IN ITS OWN SPAN: ברכו ('[the blessing with which his father] BLESSED HIM', 27:41) — Minchat Shai rules the resh with plain sheva (the bare half-vowel) 'as our custom'; SNAPSHOT points hataf patach (the compound half-vowel) — the eighth station of the resh-class split, censused from gen_46's span, now source-anchored inside its own unit. DISCREPANCY observation; both camps recorded.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:41 ('ואהרגה — the vav in sheva and the aleph in patach; Chizkuni')
claim_en: THE KILL-COHORTATIVE POINTED AS RULED: ואהרגה ('that I may KILL [my brother]') — the vav in sheva (the half-vowel) and the aleph in patach (the short a) exactly as Minchat Shai cites from the Chizkuni; SNAPSHOT letter-identical, meteg (the small stress-stroke) on the aleph.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:46 ('בחיי — the bet soft')
claim_en: THE SOFT BET OF THE WEARY LIFE: בחיי ('I am disgusted WITH MY LIFE' — Rebecca's pressure-speech) — the bet soft (no dagesh, the doubling dot) as Minchat Shai rules; the pattern bet-then-sheva with nothing between is the absence proof on SNAPSHOT's own string.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 27:46 ('קצתי — small qof; see Rabbeinu Bachya') + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on 27:46 (the qof of one hundred: the House a hundred cubits high destined for ruin; the LARGE qof of the sparrow's nest, Ps 84, David's plea that it stand)
claim_en: THE SMALL QOF (manual): קצתי ('I am DISGUSTED', 27:46) is written with a small qof per the scribal lists — the letter-size layer is uninstrumented on SNAPSHOT (standing gap; the token itself verified present at 27:46).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:5 ('את יעקב — the qof in zaqef qatan and the bet with no pashta')
claim_en: THE SEND-OFF ACCENT AS RULED: יעקב in 'and Isaac SENT JACOB away' (28:5) carries zaqef qatan (the small upright pause-accent) and no pashta (the forward-leaning accent) — SNAPSHOT letter-identical with Minchat Shai's ruling, the sliced pattern doubling as the absence proof.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:6 ('וירא עשו — with revia')
claim_en: THE FIRST SEEING RESTS ON A DOT: עשו in 'and Esau SAW that Isaac had blessed Jacob' (28:6) carries revia (the resting dot-accent) as Minchat Shai rules — the pause sits on the seer's own name.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:6 ('בברכו — the bet with wide qamatz and with the lengthening stroke in ALL the books; the resh with sheva alone in SOME of them, and in some with sheva-patach — I wrote of this at the head of Lech Lecha')
claim_en: THE LAW'S FIRST SPLIT-ATTESTED STATION: בברכו ('WHEN HE BLESSED him', 28:6) — Minchat Shai himself records the books DIVIDED on the resh: sheva alone in some, sheva-patach (hataf) in others. SNAPSHOT points hataf patach — joining the compound camp, consistent with all eight censused resh stations: the tradition's own division is external witness that the class is real. Sub-variance: the root-bet carries qamatz but NO meteg (the lengthening stroke MS reports in all books) — meteg-omission class.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:9 ('את — with maqqef')
claim_en: THE JOINED OBJECT-WORD: את before מחלת ('and he took MAHALATH', 28:9) carries the maqqef (the joining stroke) as Minchat Shai rules — SNAPSHOT stores the join on the token itself.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:9 ('מחלת — in the precise books and the early print the mem in qamatz, so Or Torah; the chet in sheva-patach in ALL the books — the printer who set plain sheva was already refuted by Or Torah')
claim_en: THE PRECISE BOOKS WIN AT MAHALATH: מחלת (Esau's Ishmaelite bride, a Torah one-time name) — mem in qamatz and chet in hataf patach exactly as the precise books and Or Torah rule; SNAPSHOT arbitrates AGAINST the printer's plain sheva. (The guttural chet takes the compound half-vowel by nature — the inverse shape of the resh-class split.)
